n: Many see a new section beginning here (chapters 56–66), focused on life in restored Zion. It opens with a practical command: be just and do right, because God’s salvation is about to arrive.

f.w: Keep ye judgment, and do justice
my salvation is near to come

n: Blessed is the person who holds firmly to this, keeps the Sabbath holy, and keeps his hands from evil. The Sabbath was a sign of the covenant, especially important for exiles without a temple.

f.w: keepeth the sabbath from polluting it

f.g: Here simply “a human being,” in parallel with “the man.”

n: Two groups who feared exclusion: foreigners who had joined the Lord, and eunuchs, who couldn’t have children and were barred from the assembly under the law of Moses. Neither should think God has shut them out.

f.g: A tree that bears no fruit—someone with no descendants to carry on his name.

n: To eunuchs who keep the Sabbath, choose what pleases God, and hold to His covenant, the Lord makes a special promise.

God will give them a memorial and name in His house better than sons and daughters—an everlasting name. The Hebrew for “a place and a name” is yad vashem, now the name of Israel’s Holocaust memorial. Covenant belonging matters more than lineage.

f.g: Hebrew yad va-shem—literally “a hand (monument) and a name.”

n: Likewise foreigners who join the Lord, love His name, keep the Sabbath, and hold to His covenant are fully welcome.

f.w: the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD

n: God will bring them to His holy mountain, make them joyful in His house of prayer, and accept their offerings, because His house will be a house of prayer for all people. Jesus quoted this when He cleansed the temple.

f.w: an house of prayer for all people

n: The Lord who gathers Israel’s outcasts will gather still others besides them. Jesus spoke of “other sheep” not of this fold—Latter-day Saints include the Nephites and others.

f.w: Yet will I gather others to him

n: A sudden shift: wild beasts are invited to come and devour. With careless shepherds, the flock is open to attack.

f.w: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour

n: Israel’s watchmen—its leaders—are blind and clueless, like guard dogs that can’t bark, always lying around and loving to sleep.
They are greedy dogs never satisfied, shepherds without understanding, each looking out only for his own profit.
Their motto: “Let’s get drunk; tomorrow will be just as good, only better!” Self-indulgent leaders who assume nothing will ever change.

f.w: to morrow shall be as this day
